claim: Alan spends seventeen hundred a month on AI compute against a category budget of a thousand, and grades Anthropic D. Moving that compute into the house is the remediation, and the same machine would make a local model a partial replacement for Google search, so two remediations wait on one purchase. What the machine is, what it costs, what it has to hold to run the models he uses, and whether it can be bought at all are recorded nowhere — the book carries the principle that local compute is the move and nothing of the move itself.

evidence:
Read across `alan/book/pages/all-about-alan/topic/pages/` and `.../question/pages/`, searching for the machine, its memory, local models, open weights and search.

What is there. `what-i-spend-on-compute`: "AI compute is my main cost, at seventeen hundred a month against a category of a thousand." `the-software-i-pay-for-every-month`: "Anthropic grades D, down from B this year", and "Gmail and Google Drive grade D on their parent's behaviour rather than on the products." `the-solar-on-the-roof` carries the whole of the plan in one clause: "Local compute in the house is the same move against depending on an AI provider, and the garden is the same move against part of the grocery bill."

What is not there. No machine is named, no memory figure, no price, no model, no vendor cadence, nothing on what would have to be true before the subscriptions could be cancelled, and nothing on search. The one self-hosting question in the book, `what-the-plan-for-self-hosting-my-anchor-is`, is about the account everything falls back on rather than about models.

The dependency between the two remediations is mine to state: the same machine serves both, so the second cannot move before the first.

Not measured: I checked no vendor's current line-up, so whether a machine that would do this can be bought today is unverified. What the models Alan runs would actually require, I did not work out.
